issues.problem: This round-1 fix was not applied. The film's last spoken line, L1520, plays over an almost black frame from 'Somewhere' (15.15) through 'suspicious' (19.1), with only a pinpoint far window (sheet frames 16.54, 18.50, 20.46). The match strikes on beat b5 at 22.09, on 'from', so 'new candles' (21.14-21.60) still lands on black and the flame only shows after the line ends.
issues.fix: Hold a dim warm desk lamp or lit far window at readable exposure (about 25% luma) from 15.0. Bring the hand and matchbox in on 'suspicious' (19.09), strike on 'new' (21.14) and catch the wick on 'candles' (21.36). Let the flame settle by 'from' (22.09) and hold it lit to the cut.

issues.problem: This was not fixed. On 'America' (3.43) and 'employed' (3.88) the threads still fan symmetrically to both shores. The new water lanterns scatter mid-frame and do not gather on the American shore. 'FIRST DEGREE: CHINA 47% · US 18%' measures 11.5px cap (legibility QA), and the unspoken 'OCT 2025 · OPEN QWEN PASSES LLAMA' tag still clutters a 9s shot.
issues.fix: From 3.43 to 4.45, swing about 70% of the thread ends visibly onto the right (US) shore and brighten that shore's lanterns while the left dims. Set the stat line to at least 22px cap, or push in on the plate during 'studied' (0.9-3.2). Cut the Qwen tag from this shot.

issues.problem: This round-1 minor was not fixed and is now repeated. Through L1527 (6.3-15.3s) the Case Board stays a static wide, and each 'rules / knowledge / Learning / data / fire / messenger' highlight is a small glow on a card about 40px wide. The film's summary of its own thesis gets no visual emphasis.
issues.fix: Make short push-ins, about 1.6x and 0.4s each, to each card on its word: rules 6.35, knowledge 7.74, Learning 9.94, data 11.77, fire 12.49, messenger 13.36, people 14.52. Pull back to the full board on 'Never one person' (16.04) so the board-to-network morph reads at full frame.

issues.problem: This was not fixed. The first frame is still an empty grey rectangle (0.5s). Two blank card-stock frames sit between text cards (11.29s, 23.50s), and the closing card still reads only 'SOURCES · published with the film' in about 14px low-contrast mono. It looks like a placeholder end card.
issues.fix: Start on the Turing card already inked, and crossfade text to text with no blank stock. Put the real sources location on the SOURCES card (URL or short-link plus 'claims.json · quotes.json') at 28px cap or more.

issues.problem: Narrated or meaningful in-scene text is still below the 22px cap minimum in many shots. Examples: ch14-s04b position tags DECISIVE/HELPS HUAWEI/SELF-DEFEATING at 11.5 (round 1 asked for twice the size) and the match lettering at 6.5; ch13-s04 '2018 A.M. TURING AWARD · Bengio · Hinton · LeCun' at about 7; ch09-s01 'LEARNED FEATURES, GIVEN DATA AND ARITHMETIC' at 15; ch05-s09b 'AAAI-84 · AUSTIN · THE DARK AGES OF AI' at 10; ch10-s14 'decoder only · Liu et al. / OpenAI GPT' chip about 12 and low contrast; ch15-s04 METR hour labels about 14. Background Case Board cards are fine as texture, but these are the subject of the line.
issues.fix: In the legibility check, tag each text as 'subject' or 'texture' and fail any subject text under 22px cap. Re-fit the listed shots by enlarging the label, or by pushing in while the line names it.

issues.problem: This is partly fixed. Hinton now has a consistent stooped profile with a hair mass, and Gebru and Bender read by hair and dress. LeCun (ch13-s04, ch15-s06), Bengio (ch13-s03, ch15-s06) and Hassabis (ch09-s03, ch15-s06) are still the same plain mannequin. No figure has rim-light edges or interior cut lines, so in ch15-s06 the three holdouts can be told apart only by their name caption.
issues.fix: In cast.ts give LeCun a broader, rounder head with glasses and a heavier build, Bengio curly hair and a slight beard line, and Hassabis a shorter, close-cropped figure. Add a 1-2px warm rim on the light-facing edge and 2 interior cut lines (collar, sleeve) to every named puppet.

issues.problem: The X-ray column is now a framed cabinet, but its face is still a flat, fully saturated cyan with app-like glyph rows. It still clashes with the amber world in ch11-s01, ch12-s01, ch12-s07, ch13-s06 and ch15-s04, and in ch12-s01 it fills half the frame.
issues.fix: Desaturate the face to about 40% and add paper grain and a soft vignette inside the frame. Dim it to about 60% except on beats where a slot lights up.

issues.problem: The banner is fixed, small and low, and inked on 'Transformer'. But allLight still fires at 7.32 ('once'), so 'every word looks at every other' (4.79-7.08) shows a single straight beam down the hall with no crossing threads. Threads leave only the first 4-5 slips.
issues.fix: Start the all-pairs threads on 'every' (4.79), building through 'every other' (6.56). Draw arcs from every slip down the hall, not only the front ones, and keep 'all at once' (7.32) as the brightness peak.

issues.problem: The push-in and the knob ticks now land on the words. The blame-formula card is still about 15% of the frame width, pinned at the right edge, at roughly 14px glyph height (frames 20.5-25.1).
issues.fix: Double the formula card and set it between the loom and the right post, inside the safe area, from 'messenger' (16.83) to 'blame' (23.98).

issues.problem: The three position tags appear in the silent gap (5.59, 6.19 and about 10.4) at 11.5px cap, and the 'COMPUTE MATTERS LESS?' lettering on the match is unreadable (6.5px) during its 1.4s life.
issues.fix: Push in on the match from 'struck' (4.20) to 'match' (4.59) so its lettering reaches 22px or more. Scale each tag to 2x and light them one at a time across 5.0-6.6, before 'China' (6.59).

issues.problem: The gap candle's label now reads, but the candle itself is still a pale ghost in the fog (frames 2.88-12.46), with no warm pool on the water. It is hard to see which taper is new.
issues.fix: Cut the fog in front of the gap candle to half, add a warm reflection on the water beneath it, and give its flame twice the glow radius of the others.

issues.problem: This was not fixed. The opening frame (tilt 0.30) is still murky, empty teal panels for about 0.6s before the study resolves.
issues.fix: Begin the tilt framed on the lit X-ray cabinet's lower slot, or cut the tilt in at 0.6s.

issues.problem: This is a new shot and it reads well through the line. The 8.5s silent tail (12.5-21.0) then drifts the camera so the bowl plate crops off the right edge, a large empty dark board fills the upper right, and a second counter '0 3 1' appears with no explanation.
issues.fix: Hold the composition locked after 'hand-made' (11.74), with the plate fully in frame, and drop the unexplained second counter. Fill the empty board with the window or with shadow, or cut the tail to about 3s.

issues.problem: The labels on this 39s shelf shot are repeatedly cropped at the frame edges ('as o / October', '26', 'VED 2026' at 22.4-34.5s). Several beats also show a near-empty shelf with stray partial props (16.5-17.0s).
issues.fix: Reframe each beat so every date and as-of tag sits inside the 5% safe area. Crossfade straight from the court beat to the settlement, with no empty-shelf frame.

issues.problem: At the 'twoAccounts' beat (16.6-17.0s) two blank grey cards stand in an almost empty frame before they ink, which reads as a placeholder.
issues.fix: Ink the 'She says she was fired' and 'Google says it accepted her resignation' cards as they appear, or bring them in already written.

issues.problem: The depth check flags only 2 planes from 8.5 to 11.0s while the camera pulls back from the door to the building.
issues.fix: Add a near occluder, such as a rain-streaked railing or a lamp post, on its own parallax layer during the pull.

issues.problem: The tall man's silhouette enters only at about 37.3s, after 'found him' ends (37.07), so 'Now, it found him' plays over an empty desk.
issues.fix: Bring the figure into the widening pool on 'found' (36.72), fully lit on 'him' (37.07), and hold 1.5s.

best_moments: ch15-s01: the Nobel hall, with chandeliers, arched windows and a dense silhouette audience. The medallion turns toward Hopfield on his name, and the phone glows on 'phone' (9.37). It is still the film's closest match to the reference craft.
ch12-s06: November 2022. The cyan box goes amber and swings open like a door on 'door', then the camera pulls back to one warm window in a cold city.
ch12-s03 (restaged): the ledger under the lamp, written in pen on 'FTX' and 'billions', then Bard, LLaMA, GPT-4 and Claude chips pinned on each name. Clean, period-true and synced to the words.

ch08-s05: the cathedral of stencils. The cat in the rose window becomes edges, then textures, then an eye, then the cat, with each tier lighting on its word. The halls card '55·27·13·13·13 → 4096·4096·1000' lands on 'halls'.
ch12-s08: the ChatGPT door with the stampede silhouettes, then the building's windows lighting in order: CODE RED, Microsoft and the Meta lantern leak.
ch13-s02: Hinton walks from the candle's pool to the rim, where a pale ghost of his younger self sits at a desk.
ch09-s03 (fixed): a real 19x19 board, with the move-37 shoulder hit ringed '1 in 10,000' on 'thirty-seven'.
ch15-s07: Widrow's paper lantern on a snowy sill under the moon, with 'I never got over it.' Restrained and moving.
